A field toolkit for protection engineers. It connects to Power System Protection Relays over the IEC 61850 MMS protocol to retrieve and analyse COMTRADE fault records, locate line faults from the records of both line ends, browse an IED\'s live data model, and continuously monitor measurements and alarms across a whole fleet of substations.
Work through the chapters in order, from set-up to fault analysis. Tap a chapter to see its steps, then use the buttons below the steps to jump straight to the screen it covers.
Permissions, network and basic settings before connecting to a relay.

1. Grant the permissions the app asks for: Notifications (update news), "All files access" (so DFR files in Download/DFR and other folders can be read) and "Install unknown apps" the first time you install an update.
2. Connect the phone to the relay network: the office intranet or FortiClient VPN. FortiClient can be opened from the Home side menu, and is offered automatically when the intranet check fails.
3. Open Settings and check the MMS port (normally 102), the intranet IP used for the network check, ping counts, monitoring interval and app language.
4. Have a configuration backup from a colleague or an old phone? Import it now with Import Configuration - the device list, monitoring points, relay templates and line database are filled in at once.
One relay database, so IPs and names never have to be typed twice.

1. Tap + to add a device: UPT, ULTG, substation (GI), bay, device, IP, relay brand and type.
2. For many devices at once, tap Import CSV. Download the template first - column order: UPT, ULTG, NAMA GI, BAY, DEVICE, IP, MERK, TYPE. When a CSV IP is already listed with different data, the app asks OVERWRITE or SKIP.
3. Narrow the list with the filters, in order: UPT, ULTG, GI, BAY, then DEVICE.
4. Tap the Ping all icon at the top to check every device's online/offline state and port 102 (IEC 61850).
5. Tap a device for quick actions: Ping, IED Explorer, DFR Download, Edit or Delete. Export CSV to share the list with colleagues.
Fetching disturbance records (COMTRADE) straight from the relay over MMS / IEC 61850.

1. From the Device List tap a device and then DFR Download, or open DFR Download and pick a device with the list icon (or type the IP).
2. Leave the INTRANET switch on so the network is checked first. If connecting fails, try another Profile (Default, ABB/GE, Schneider).
3. Tap CONNECT. The app detects the relay brand and scans the record folders automatically.
4. Records are listed newest first, 50 per page. Use Prev/Next, or tap the page info to jump to a page.
5. Tap DOWNLOAD on one record, or choose Bulk (the N newest records) / Single (record number N) and start the download. The partner files (.cfg, .dat, .hdr, or .zip and h.zip) come along.
6. When done, choose OPEN (straight into the DFR Viewer), open the folder, or share the files.
Files are saved in Download/DFR/<GI>_<BAY> and also show up in Download History and in FL Double Ended\'s local record list.
Managing the DFR files already on the phone.

1. Files are grouped per GI_BAY folder - tap a folder to see its contents.
2. Tap a .cfg file to open it in the DFR Viewer.
3. Share a folder's contents with another app, or delete files/folders you no longer need.
4. If the list is empty on Android 11 or later, grant the "All files access" permission it asks for.
Reading Records in the DFR Viewer
Viewing waveforms, measuring fault values and making a report.

1. Open a record from Download History, from the Open button after a download, or with the folder icon: pick a .cfg file, or a .zip/.rar archive holding the .cfg + .dat.
2. From WhatsApp, Telegram or a file manager: tap the .cfg/.dat/.zip/.rar file, choose Open with, then DFR Viewer.
3. In the mapping dialog, match the channels to the relay template. The mapping can be changed later from the settings menu, Edit Configuration.
4. Drag the T1/T2 cursors to read time and value differences. Lock zoom and cursors so every channel moves together.
5. Fill in the assessment (title, phases, values), then export to PDF or DOWNLOAD IMG. Companion files (.hdr/.inf/.xml) open from the settings menu.
The DFR Viewer reads ASCII .dat files. BINARY records can still be analysed in FL Double Ended.
Line lengths and impedances, used by FL Double Ended.

1. In Excel, save the conductor data sheet as CSV, then Import it in the Line Database. A summary shows how many lines were added or updated.\n2. Or add a line by hand: GI, bay, remote GI, length, R1/X1 and R0/X0 per km.\n3. FL Double Ended picks this data automatically when a line connects both substations, and it is included in the configuration export.
Computing the fault distance from the relay records at both line ends.

1. At END A pick the substation and line relay, then get a record: Download from relay (the record closest in time to the other end is marked), or Local file - a stored record, a .cfg file (its .dat in the same folder comes along) or a .zip/.rar archive. Substation or relay not in the Device List? Tap Enter manually to type the substation name, bay and relay IP.
2. Do the same at END B. From WhatsApp too: Open with, FL Double Ended, then choose end A or B.
3. Check the Channel mapping (Va, Vb, Vc, Ia, Ib, Ic) of each end. Tick Invert current polarity when that end's CT is reversed.
4. Pick the line from the Line Database, or fill in length, R1, X1, R0, X0. Then tap Analyze.
5. Read the result: distance from each substation, fault type, method comparison, fault-point voltage chart and phasor tables. Read any warnings too (polarity, fault outside the line, line data).
6. Adjust the vector synchronisation slider if needed, then Save the result (PDF report + history) or Share the report.
The last analysis is kept: when FL Double Ended is opened again, the records, mapping, line data and result come back as they were.
Watching relay values and states periodically.

1. Open the IED Explorer, enter the relay IP (or pick it from the list), and browse its Logical Devices, Logical Nodes and Data Attributes.
2. Tap + next to a value to add it to Monitoring - set its name, type, unit and multiplier.
3. For many relays of the same type, build a Relay Template once and apply it to several devices at once with the Template button in IED Monitoring.
4. In IED Monitoring, refresh all devices or just one. Tap a point's edit icon to set upper/lower alarm limits.
5. The Substation Status Map shows every device's online/offline state per substation on one screen.
Keeping your data safe and the app up to date.

1. In Settings, Export Configuration regularly: one file with the device list, monitoring points, relay templates, node definitions and line database. Share it so colleagues work with the same data.
2. Import Configuration merges that file into your data without overwriting anything already there.
3. When a new version is released an update notification appears - tap it to download and install. Past notifications are under the bell icon on Home.
4. Check for updates by hand with the Check Update button at the bottom of this page.
Quick fixes for the most common problems.

1. Can't connect to a relay: make sure the VPN/intranet is on, check Ping and port 102 in the Device List, then try another connection Profile.
2. ".cfg + .dat pair not found": pick the .cfg from its folder (the .dat comes along), send both in one .zip/.rar, and make sure "All files access" is granted.
3. Password-protected RAR archives can't be opened - ask the sender to resend without a password.
4. Doubtful FL Double Ended result: read its warnings, check CT polarity and line data, and make sure both records are of the same event.
5. Colour theme and dark mode are changed from the Home side menu; the app language in Settings.
6. What every button on every screen does is explained in Help.

Two-ended fault location from 2 relay DFRs
Channel mapping incomplete – tap Channel mapping
Enter whole-line totals (Ω, µS) instead of per km

Primary-side line impedance. The two-ended method only needs Z1 (R1, X1); Z0 is used for the single-ended cross-check and the fault resistance of earth faults. Fill B1 for long lines (over ~150 km) to switch to the distributed (hyperbolic) line model. Leave the window empty to let the most stable fault window be picked automatically.

|V| (sequence used by the main method, kV) computed along the line from each end using that end\'s own voltage and current. Both curves can only agree at the real fault point – their crossing is the fault location.

Main method: unsynchronised two-ended fault location (IEEE C37.114-2014; Novosel et al. 1996; Tziouvaras, Roberts & Benmouyal 2001).

1. The COMTRADE records of the line relays at substation A and B are read (ASCII, BINARY, BINARY32, FLOAT32, zip) and converted to primary values.

2. Fault inception is detected in each record with a cycle-to-cycle superimposed detector.

3. Fundamental phasors are estimated by a one-cycle least-squares fit (fundamental + 2nd/3rd harmonic + DC trend), so the decaying DC offset of the fault current does not bias them.

4. Symmetrical components are calculated. Unbalanced faults use the negative sequence (V2, I2); three-phase faults use the superimposed positive sequence (fault minus pre-fault).

5. The fault-point voltage is computed by walking the line model from each end: |V2A − m·Z1·I2A| = |V2B − (1−m)·Z1·I2B|. Only magnitudes are compared, so the two relay clocks do NOT need to be synchronised, and the result is not affected by fault resistance, load current or zero-sequence mutual coupling. Long lines can use the distributed (hyperbolic) model.

6. The equation is solved on several consecutive windows; the final result is their median and the spread is shown as ± km.

7. Cross-checks: two-ended positive sequence, two-ended time-synchronised (valid only with GPS-synchronised relays) and single-ended Takagi from each end. A large difference between methods means the data should be checked.

8. Vector synchronisation (voltage only): substation A is fixed at its highest fault current and record B is shifted in time until the V1 and V0 angles of both ends agree, starting from the detected fault inceptions so both records show the same moment. The shift can be adjusted with a slider; the time-synchronised two-ended location is recalculated with the aligned vectors. It assumes both ends' voltages are close in angle during the fault, so the unsynchronised method stays the default main result.

Requirements: both records belong to the same event, both CTs measure current flowing into the line, and the line impedance is correct. Typical accuracy is 1–2 percent of line length, set mainly by the accuracy of Z1.

Travelling-wave location is not used: relay DFRs sample at 1–4 kHz, far too slow for travelling waves.

Takes one COMTRADE record from the line relay at each end (GI A and GI B) and calculates the fault distance with the unsynchronised two-ended negative-sequence method, which needs no clock synchronisation between the relays and is not affected by fault resistance or load. Single-ended Takagi and other methods are shown alongside as a cross-check.

Explains the calculation method step by step.

1. Under END A pick the substation and the line relay, then tap Download from relay (or Local file) and choose the fault record.
2. Do the same under END B - the record closest in time to END A is marked with a star.
3. Fill in the line length and R1/X1 (per km, or switch on whole-line totals). Add R0/X0 for earth-fault cross-checks and B1 for long lines.
4. Tap Analyze fault location.

1. The big numbers are the distance from each substation; the ± value is the spread over several fault windows.
2. The method comparison shows every result as km from END A with its difference to the main result.
3. The chart shows the fault-point voltage computed from each end - the crossing is the fault.
4. Tap Share report to send the result as text.

1. Read the {ic:warning} warnings under the result.
2. If one end sees the fault in REVERSE, tap the button to invert that end's current polarity and re-analyze.
3. Check that both records belong to the same event and that the line impedance is primary-side ohms.
4. Open {ic:settings} Channel mapping if a channel was detected wrongly or the record is in secondary values without ratios.
